detail: Known: Berkeley Lab's review of rate designs for large loads (https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/rate_designs_large_loads_2026.08.10.pdf, August 2026) gives a median minimum billing demand of 80 percent of contracted demand across the tariffs it reviewed; FactSet (https://insight.factset.com/minimum-billing-demand-a-key-component-in-u.s.-data-center-tariffs, November 2025) gives 80 to 100 percent. Ours: 80 percent at the median of 11 filings, from 75 to 100 percent. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67664, May 2026) gives Virginia's commercial sales up nearly 30 million MWh from 2019 to 2025 using EIA-861M for 2025; no publisher found printing Virginia Electric and Power Company's own commercial sales by year. Ours: 60.09 TWh in 2025 against 41.54 TWh in 2017. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: CAISO's market monitor (https://www.caiso.com/documents/2024-special-report-on-battery-storage-may-29-2025.pdf) and the IEA give batteries' share of energy at the peak hour (24 percent in 2024, IEA) and of energy in net peak hours (about 9 percent in 2024); no publisher found printing the fleet's capacity against the mean of the ten highest days. Ours: 46.6 percent in 2025 against 0.6 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: E3's ERCOT market update (https://ethree.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/E3-2024-ERCOT-Market-Update.pdf) and Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/ercot-power-prices-2024-energy-arbitrage-ancillary-services-hub-load-zone-west-north-south-houston-panhandle, February 2025) describe a midday dip in ERCOT prices as solar grew; no publisher found printing the mean hour of the day's cheapest real-time hour by year. Ours: 10.7 hours after local midnight in 2025 against 6.0 in 2015 at the North hub. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/ercot-power-prices-2024-energy-arbitrage-ancillary-services-hub-load-zone-west-north-south-houston-panhandle) says West Texas prices sat below the hub from 9 AM to 4 PM in 2024 as solar rose; no publisher found printing the West zone's midday price as a share of its all-hours mean by year. Ours: 48.9 percent in 2025 against 128.9 percent in 2015. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/ercot-bess-operations-battery-dispatch-one-hour-two-hour-spread-compression-revenue-capture-eolian-engie-sced-offer-curves, June 2025) reports ERCOT's real-time top-bottom one-hour spread at 98 USD per MWh on average in 2024, 61 percent below 2023, as batteries grew; no publisher found printing the evening price as a share of the all-hours mean by year since 2015. Ours: 161.0 percent in 2025 against 109.5 percent in 2015 at the South hub. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Modo Energy and EnergyGPS (https://www.energygps.com/Newsletter/b/Blog-Lonely-Star-Batteries-3435685) write that batteries still capture a positive spread every day while the ceiling has come down; no publisher found printing the share of days with a 50 USD spread by year. Ours: 84.1 percent of days in 2025 against 28.8 percent in 2015 in the West zone. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

New as far as found: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=63344, 2024) expected ERCOT's large flexible loads (mostly crypto mining and data centers) to use 54 billion kWh in 2025; no publisher found printing ERCOT's load factor by year. Ours: 66.6 percent in 2025 against 58.8 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: ISO New England's market monitor, Fall 2025 quarterly report (https://www.iso-ne.com/static-assets/documents/100032/a04_mc_2026_02_10-11_imm_fall_2025_qmr_presentation.pdf), says New England was a net exporter in the fall of 2025 for the first time in at least two decades, 33 MW an hour on average; EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67105) counts days of net exports to Canada. Ours: the share of 2025's hours in which New England exported on net, 27.8 percent against 0.05 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

New as far as found: EIA prints the volatility of the Henry Hub front-month future (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66984 gives the 2025 spot range, 2.65 to 9.86 USD per MMBtu); no publisher found printing the median absolute daily change of the spot price by year. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook (https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/perspectives/2024/09-gulfofmexico/article.php) expects federal Gulf gas of about 1.7 to 1.8 Bcf a day in 2025, a different measure (marketed) from BOEM's lease reports that the draft sums (2,079 million cubic feet a day in 2025 against 14,196 in 1996). Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67664, 2026) gives the Dominion zone's summer peak of 23,905 MW in 2025, 23 percent above 2019; FactSet (https://insight.factset.com/data-center-power-demand-begins-to-surge-across-the-u.s, September 2025) says Dominion's average hourly load was up about 30 percent on 2019 through September 2025. Ours gives the full year: a mean hour of 15,403 MW in 2025 against 11,687 MW in 2019 (31.8 percent). Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: ERCOT's Permian Basin reliability plan (https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2024/06/28/Reliability-Plan-For-The-Permian-Basin-Region.pdf) gives Far West peak demand growth of about 11 percent a year for a decade, and ERCOT's board item of February 2026 (https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2026/02/04/13-Far-West-Load-Growth-and-Transmission-Timing-Issues.pdf) puts the area's reliable load-serving capability at about 9,500 MW. Ours: a mean hour of 7,606 MW in 2025 against 3,682 MW in 2020. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: the same ERCOT documents (https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2026/02/04/13-Far-West-Load-Growth-and-Transmission-Timing-Issues.pdf) give about 9,500 MW of reliable load-serving capability in Far West Texas; no publisher found printing the zone's 99th-percentile hour by year. Ours: 8,763 MW in 2025 against 4,337 MW in 2020. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=63684, 2024) reports Hydro-Quebec's deliveries into New York falling in 2023 with drought; Grid Status (https://blog.gridstatus.io/more-hqs-than-answers-hydro-quebec-isone-nyiso-ties/) says NYISO's net trade with Canada in January to August 2025 was a quarter of 2022's. Ours gives the yearly mean hourly flow from Canada to New York, 211 MW in 2025 against 1,992 MW in 2019. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is the Census Bureau's own value put in place (Construction Spending, https://www.census.gov/construction/c30/historical_data.html); Statista (https://www.statista.com/statistics/1559548/private-sector-data-center-construction-completed-us) prints about 41 billion USD for 2025 from an earlier vintage, and an analysis of Census tables says data center spending passed office construction in December 2025. Ours: 49.74 billion USD in 2025 (current vintage). Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Electric Power Annual table 11.3 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_11_03.html) prints SAIDI by state with and without major events; its 2025 Nebraska figure was not visible in the search result. Ours: 542.8 minutes a customer in 2025 against 67.9 in 2015, major event days included. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA's own table of crude exports by destination (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/pet_move_expc_a_EPC0_EEX_mbblpd_a.htm, opened 19 November 2026) prints 862 thousand barrels a day for 2025; EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67324) says the Netherlands took more US crude in 2025 while Europe as a whole took less. The draft repeats EIA's own series.

Known: EIA's own table (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/pet_move_expc_a_EPC0_EEX_mbblpd_a.htm, opened 19 November 2026) prints total crude exports of 3,961 thousand barrels a day for 2025; EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67324) headlines the first annual fall since 2021. The draft repeats EIA's own series and headline.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67664, 2026) says Virginia's commercial sales rose by nearly 30 million MWh from 2019 to 2025, faster than any state but Texas, tied to data centers; EPRINC (https://eprinc.org/virginia-electricity-demand-growth-the-case-of-data-centers/) gives 67.5 TWh of commercial demand in 2023. Ours adds the long view from EIA's State Energy Data System: 78.7 TWh in 2024 against 28.1 TWh in 1990. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA (reported by Oil and Gas Journal, https://ogj.com/general-interest/economics-markets/news/55324404/us-exports-record-natural-gas-volumes-to-mexico-in-2025-amid-growing-demand, October 2025) gives pipeline exports to Mexico of 6.4 Bcf a day in 2024, a record in data from 1975, and 7.5 Bcf a day in May 2025; ours, 2,423 Bcf in 2025 (6.6 Bcf a day), is EIA's own annual series. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67484, 2026) gives US LNG exports of 15.1 Bcf a day in 2025, up 26 percent; no publisher found printing them as a share of dry production. Ours: 14.0 percent in 2025 against 0.1 percent in 2015. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: EIA's 2025 averages, residential 17.30 and industrial 8.62 cents a kWh (EIA Electric Power Monthly table 5.6.A, https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/epm_table_grapher.php?t=epmt_5_6_a), a gap of 86.8 USD per MWh against ours of 87.7; Berkeley Lab's Retail Price Trends, 2026 edition (https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/retail_price_trends_2026_edition_julyupdate.pdf), describes the gap widening. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is EIA's own net interstate receipts series for Pennsylvania (Natural Gas Annual, table S40, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/Annual/pdf/table_S40.pdf, gives the 2024 interstate deliveries of 5,891 Bcf); the draft repeats EIA's own series. Seen in search results, page not opened.

New as far as found: no publisher found printing the yearly mean of Gulf Coast gasoline spot less WTI; EIA's Today in Energy prints New York Harbor gasoline crack spreads (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66964) and RBN Energy the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 spread (https://rbnenergy.com/daily-posts/analyst-insight/usgc-3-2-1-crack-spread-cools-remains-strong), both other measures. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: TVA's own statements, reported by the American Public Power Association (https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/tva-sets-new-all-time-power-demand-record-power-system-remains-stable, January 2025) and Power Engineering (https://www.power-eng.com/business/historic-gas-build-drives-tvas-strategy-as-utility-sets-new-load-records/), give a winter peak hour of 35,319 MW on 22 January 2025 (later 35,430 MW) against a summer peak of 32,318 MW in August 2025. Ours adds the ratio of the five highest winter days to the five highest summer days, by year since 2019 (113.9 percent in 2025). Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is the Census Bureau's own published revenue of data processing and hosting firms (NAICS 518); FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/REVEF518ALLEST) carries the Service Annual Survey series (310.7 billion USD for 2022). The draft repeats the publisher's own total. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66704, November 2025) gives CAISO batteries at 4.9 GW on average from 5 to 9 PM in May and June 2025 and gas generation down 18 percent from 2020; no publisher found printing gas's share of 5 to 10 PM generation by year. One search result (Grid Status and EIA notes) says CAISO changed how it collects natural gas output in December 2023, so the 2019 and 2025 figures may not be comparable: this would make the draft wrong. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the California Public Utilities Commission's resource tracking data, December 2025 release (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cpuc-website/divisions/energy-division/documents/summer-2021-reliability/tracking-energy-development/resource-tracking-data-december-2025-release.pdf), lists 15,762 MW of battery projects online, from CAISO's Master Generating Capability List; Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/caiso-battery-fleet-2025-q4-15gw-interconnection-queue-standalone-colocated, 24 March 2026) gives 15.7 GW. Ours: 15,777 MW. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67205, 2026) gives 43.6 GW of operating battery storage at the end of 2025 and 15 GW added in 2025. Ours: 43,678 MW. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Ascend Analytics (https://www.ascendanalytics.com/blog/emerging-energy-reliability-risks-and-needs-in-ercot-its-not-an-afternoon-problem-anymore) and Grid Status (https://blog.gridstatus.io/ercot-record-july-2026/) describe ERCOT's tightest hours moving to the evening when solar has faded; no publisher found printing solar's output in the tightest hours as a share of capacity. Ours adds the figure by year, 71.1 percent in 2019 against 5.0 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66464, October 2025) gives ERCOT solar at 24 GW on average from noon to 1 PM in summer 2025 against 12 GW in summer 2023, and gas's midday share falling from 50 to 37 percent; no publisher found printing solar's share of 11 AM to 4 PM generation by year. Ours adds 32.4 percent in 2025 against 2.5 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Berkeley Lab's Queued Up, 2026 edition (https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/queued_up_2026_edition.pdf), prints the median months from request to commercial operation by year (61 months for projects built in 2025, all types) and by type; the draft reads Berkeley Lab's own queue data, so it repeats the publisher's measure. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: the California Air Resources Board's Monthly LCFS Credit Transfer Activity, September 2026 (https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/September%202026%20-%20Monthly%20LCFS%20Credit%20Transfer%20Activity.pdf), gives a calendar 2025 average of 60 USD a credit (volume weighted); ours, the mean of weekly prices, is 59.26 USD. Seen in search results, page not opened.
